task: Construct an exact-marginal, bounded-vector-discrepancy distribution on arbitrary bipartite perfect matchings, with compressed finite support and full costs.
overall_status: internally_derived_composition_candidate; depends on a source-reported rational signing theorem; no novelty or priority claim

input_contract.graph: Explicit labelled bipartite graph with n vertices on each shore; parallel labelled edges are permitted.
input_contract.marginals: Explicit rational x_e >= 0 with incident-edge sum exactly one at every vertex.
input_contract.features: Explicit rational A in Q^(d x |E|).
input_contract.signer: Deterministic rational Komlos signing routine: for rational columns of Euclidean norm <= 1, return signs with infinity discrepancy < 99.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For every explicit bipartite graph G=(L,R,E), |L|=|R|=n>=1, rational feasible perfect-matching marginal x, and rational feature matrix A, the implementation computes B*=min(B0,2n max_e ceil(||A_e||_2)), with B0=sum_{e,j}|A[j,e]|, and, conditional on the rational <99 Komlos signer, outputs a rational law on at most |E|+1 perfect matchings M with E[1_M]=x and ||A(1_M-x)||_infinity<100B* for every positive atom. Both terms in B* are explicit all-cycle upper bounds, so no cycle-norm oracle is required. Unit Euclidean edge columns give B*<=2n. More generally, the proof permits any supplied rational upper bound B on all simple-cycle feature norms.
claims.proof_path: PROOF.md; implementation of the non-signing compiler components in matching_dyadic_compiler.py
claims.novelty_boundary: Composition of exact network-flow decomposition, systematic unbiased dyadic weight rounding, Eulerian odd-support cycle halving, Li's Komlos signing, and exact affine-dependence compression. Not externally validated and not a novelty or priority claim. Astra P-round already records a more general exact-mean Boolean-polytope theorem under strong optimization; this is a matching-specific explicit compiler and cycle-feature bound.
claims.costs: At most |E| exact bipartite matching calls for the seed; K=ceil(log2(2sn))=O(log(n|E|)) levels for s<=|E|; at most |E|+1 active atoms and |E| cycle columns per Li call; Li source-reported cost on d x t columns: O(t^2 log t) updates, O(dt+t^(omega+2)log^3 t) arithmetic/comparisons, polynomial rational-bit complexity; polynomial-size exact rational affine dependence elimination at every level. Output has at most |E|+1 atoms with polynomial-bit weights. The complete polynomial runtime relies on the imported Li signer; the callback is not reimplemented in this workspace.
claims.falsifier: A feasible input where systematic rounding fails exact mean/cardinality; an odd-numerator support with an odd degree; an alternating cycle sum that fails degree cancellation; a child outside the matching polytope; any exact compression that changes total mass/mean; or a verified Li signer failure under the exact unit-column premise.
claims.next_gate: Independently review/formally replay the Li rational signer and execute an exact end-to-end fixture through that backend. Compare the cycle parameter B with actual k(P) on explicit instances without asserting equality.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Given x=sum_{i=1}^s lambda_i 1_{M_i}, rational lambda_i>=0 summing to one, and D=2^K>=2sn, systematic rounding of the lambda_i to adjacent multiples of 1/D produces an explicit law on at most s+1 dyadic matching barycenters y with E[y]=x and ||A(y-x)||_infinity<=B/2 whenever every alternating cycle feature vector has Euclidean norm at most B.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard systematic sampling combined with the cycle decomposition bound; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: O(s) breakpoints and exact rational arithmetic of polynomial bit length; D has O(log(sn)) bits.
claims.falsifier: Directly violate the floor-difference 0/1 property, the exact cardinality R, or E[b_i]=f_i for a rational input fixture.
claims.next_gate: The finite wrapper tests do not replace an integrated test with Li's polynomial signer.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For y=b/2^k in the bipartite degree-one polytope, the odd-numerator support is Eulerian. If its edge-disjoint even-cycle decomposition is C_1,...,C_t and Li signs the columns A u_C/B with infinity discrepancy <99, then y^+=y+s/2^k and y^-=y-s/2^k are feasible degree-one points on the denominator-2^(k-1) grid, midpoint y, and each feature increment is <99B/2^k.
claims.novelty_boundary: Graph cycles are only feasible circulations for the current degree equations and box constraints; no claim says they are actual edges of the perfect-matching polytope.
claims.costs: At most |E| cycle columns per atom; exact cycle arithmetic polynomial in graph size and input bits.
claims.falsifier: Any odd-degree vertex in the odd-numerator support, non-even cycle in a bipartite graph, nonzero signed degree at a vertex, or infeasible child point.
claims.next_gate: End-to-end exact fixture through the reported Li backend.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Li arXiv:2609.30044v1, Theorem 1.1, states that a rational matrix with Euclidean column norms at most one admits a deterministic algorithm returning signs with infinity discrepancy <99; the source reports O(t^2 log t) updates, O(dt+t^(omega+2)log^3 t) arithmetic/comparisons, and polynomial bit complexity for rational input of total encoding length L_in.
claims.proof_path: Li primary arXiv HTML, Theorem 1.1 and Section 11.3; https://arxiv.org/html/2609.30044v1
claims.novelty_boundary: Used as an imported ordinary signing subroutine only. It does not itself provide prescribed nonzero means or the matching law.
claims.costs: Source-reported real arithmetic/update bounds and polynomial rational-bit complexity; actual local implementation is absent.
claims.falsifier: A correction to the source theorem's column norm premise, strict <99 constant, rational-bit statement, or deterministic polynomial-time implementation claim.
claims.next_gate: Independent mathematical review and local implementation or formal replay.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: Any rational law on feasible points of a polytope in R^E can be compressed by exact affine dependence to at most E+1 existing support points while preserving its mean; if all input points satisfy an atomwise discrepancy bound, the compressed law does also.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard rational Caratheodory elimination; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: At most E+1 exact linear dependence eliminations per level on matrices of at most (E+1) x 2(E+1). At denominator 2^k, a primitive integer dependence coefficient is bounded by r! 2^(kr), r<=E+1. A common probability denominator Q grows to 2Q on branching/merging and to Q|a_i| per elimination, so across K levels output weight bit length is O(L_x+K E^2(K+log(E+1))); no fresh LP is required for polynomial bit growth.
claims.falsifier: A dependence update that changes total mass or barycenter, or produces a negative retained weight.
claims.next_gate: No separate compression gap found; integrated Li backend review remains outstanding.

claims.exact_statement_and_assumptions: For C_(2k), center edge marginals and scalar alternating actual-edge features +1,-1 force probability 1/2 on each of the two perfect matchings, whose feature errors are +k and -k. Thus unit edge-column norms do not permit a graph-independent all-atom discrepancy constant; the cycle feature norm is 2k.
